cause: A visually occluded PDF text block could be marked success by extraction and bypass the pending-only human review, then enter indexed evidence.
change: The authenticated review API and UI now offer a separate paged view of success-marked text within an existing review-required job, with the immutable original and page coordinate available for comparison.
An owner may exclude a success-marked block as decoration with a revisioned, source/artifact-bound judgment; retaining it can only preserve the exact original extracted text, not substitute new text.

Reviewed extraction requires every originally pending block to be resolved and validates every optional success-block override. It writes receipt-linked derived bytes without changing the original artifact, and verifies the same decisions again before indexing.

checks.focusedVitest: 4 files, 29 tests passed: reviewed artifact, visual candidates, binary registration and authenticated review API
checks.browser: 2 Playwright component flows passed at 1366x900 and 390x844: success-tab source text, coordinates, page preview, exclusion save, return to pending completion and no horizontal overflow; screenshots visually inspected

sourceBoundary: The ITU PDF directly drove this repair and is now development/regression only; its FWA conflict question is excluded from fresh independent Gold.
limits: The browser check used a bundled component and synthetic authenticated API responses; the actual running candidate and production service were not exercised.
This review path applies while a job is already review-required. A file with only success-marked blocks can still bypass human review, so a general prepublication visibility gate remains open.
Production Web and knowledge services have not loaded this change; no production document was modified.
